$comment: Shared VfAccordion cases. Plain data only: no Vue, no PHP, no renderer objects. Each adapter maps these neutral fields onto its own API. The vocabulary is the historical Vue contract at fd793696f50d3be0fcd3788f0f8f751c63869963. The first catalog for a component that owns a control: every case declares `componentInteractive`, the number of controls the component itself renders - one trigger per instance - and `consumerInteractive`, the number a consumer put in a slot that actually reaches the DOM in that state. An interaction case names the action, the semantic effect it must produce on every target, and the initial case whose DOM the result must converge on. scripts/ci/accordion-coverage.mjs is what stops the list eroding.

propVocabulary.open: boolean | undefined, default undefined. The controlled state; wins whenever defined. A Vue consumer pairs it with update:open (v-model:open). The Razor adapter reads it as the initial state and toggles on its own, because a server-rendered accordion has no parent to ask.
propVocabulary.defaultOpen: boolean, default false. Seeds the uncontrolled state; read once.
propVocabulary.title: string, default undefined. Rendered in a bare span inside the trigger unless a trigger slot replaces it. An absent or empty title still renders the empty span.
propVocabulary.disabled: boolean, default false. The native disabled attribute on the trigger and nothing else. Does not close an open accordion.

contentVocabulary.trigger: The trigger slot. `text` replaces the title span; `control` is a real consumer link inside the trigger, unmarked - a control the consumer placed, not the trigger.
contentVocabulary.body: The default slot, rendered inside div.vf-accordion__content-inner only while open. `text` is plain text; `markup` is rich consumer markup; `control` is a real consumer button; `accordion` nests a second accordion with its own title, defaultOpen and text.
contentVocabulary.group: A list of sibling accordions rendered side by side in one case, each with its own props. The case-level title is ignored.

ownershipVocabulary.componentInteractive: The exact number of controls the component itself renders in this case: one button.vf-accordion__trigger per instance. Asserted on every target against the measured component-owned controls, and their tag identity against the profile - a div with role=button is not the trigger.
ownershipVocabulary.consumerInteractive: The exact number of consumer controls that reach the DOM in this case's initial state. Zero when a slot with a control is closed, because v-if renders nothing.

interactionVocabulary.$comment: A case with an `interaction` is driven in the browser with real pointer and key events, then re-measured: the snapshot, the DOM and the accessibility tree are all taken again after the transition has settled.
interactionVocabulary.steps: clickButton (a real pointer click at the element's centre; `index` picks a trigger in a group or a nested pair), focusButton, pressKey with Enter or Space.
interactionVocabulary.expect: Claims checked against the snapshot on every target: `activates` is whether a native click reached the trigger, `expanded` and `expandedStates` are the trigger's aria-expanded, `panelPresent`/`panelCount` whether the region is in the DOM, `consumerControlCount` the consumer controls after the action, `focusRole` where focus ended, `settled` that no inline transition declaration remained.
interactionVocabulary.matches: The initial case whose DOM the post-interaction DOM must equal on the same target. A toggle has to land on the state a fresh render produces, not on a hybrid with leftover inline styles or a hidden panel.
interactionVocabulary.consumerInteractive: The consumer-control budget after the action, when it differs from the case's initial budget.
